# Root list test vectors

Fixtures for the [signed root list and the CA bundle](../../docs/reference/root-list.md): root lists that a host must accept or refuse, given the list it already holds, and CA bundles with their trust sequence, with the expected outcome and reason code of each in `v1/manifest.json`.

The roots are the test roots of the [hand-off vectors](../hand-off/README.md): A and B are active, C is a root that some lists add, Z is on no list. `pki/` holds copies of their certificates and OpenPGP primaries, `removals/` the removal authorisation of A, B and C as the holder would store them, and the list `seq7-a` is the root list of the trust sequence the hand-off answers carry (7). Everything under `v1/` is public material made with throw-away software keys by `../hand-off/generate.py`, in the same run as the hand-off set; no private key is kept. The record digests in the lists are made up. A change to a vector that flips its outcome is a new format version (a new directory).

`just check-vectors` checks that the manifest names every tracked file, that the pins match the root files, that every list carries the signatures of its `signers` and that they verify except in the tampered one, that every removal authorisation is valid except the one a case refuses, and that each bundle holds the roots it names under its trust sequence.

## What the cases add

- **The same list again** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 50; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). After a root left, a list that is byte for byte the held one passes: `same-list-again-after-a-revoke` (`seq8-b-without-a`, which carries a removal) and `same-list-again-after-a-retire` (`seq8-ab-without-a`, which the retired root signed). Checks 8 to 10 do not run for it; the clock check does. `same-list-again-with-an-unknown-signer-beside-a-trusted-one` is accepted: the held list again, with a second signature by Z, a root key on no list (the bytes of `root-list.json` are those of `seq7-a`); `same-list-again-after-its-expiry` is refused with `expired` (the host also warns `held-expired`).
- **The dates of a list** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 49; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). In every list of this set, and of the SSH CA key list set, `expires_at` is exactly 13 calendar months after `signed_at` (the same day and time, or the last day of the month), and no case has a candidate that is signed after its clock; no list had to be corrected. Three lists break one rule each, and the manifest names the break in their `flaw`: `seq7-a-expires-13m1s` and `seq7-a-expires-12m` (`expires_at-not-13-months`) and `seq7-a-signed-in-the-future`, signed one second after the clock of its case (`signed_at-after-clock`). Each is refused with `malformed`, in the cases `expires-13-months-and-a-second-after-signing`, `expires-12-months-after-signing` and `signed-after-the-clock`, which give their clock. `update` is the case at the boundary: `seq7-a` is signed at the clock. The end of a month: lists signed on 2026-01-31, 2027-01-30 and 2028-02-29 expire on 2027-02-28, 2028-02-29 and 2029-03-29 and are accepted (`signed-on-the-31st-of-january`, `signed-on-the-30th-of-january-before-a-leap-year`, `signed-on-a-leap-day`, each at its own signing time); the lists with the expiry that a plain month addition gives (2027-03-03 and 2028-03-01) are refused with `malformed` (`expires-by-plain-month-addition-from-the-31st`, `expires-by-plain-month-addition-from-the-30th`).
- **CA bundles** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 52; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). A case with `bundle` also checks that CA bundle against the candidate list (`--ca-bundle`): `ca-bundle-of-the-list` and `ca-bundle-after-a-revoke` are accepted. A bundle whose certificate holds the key of root A but does not verify with its own key (signed by the key of Z) is `ca-bundle-7-signed-by-another-key`, and one that verifies with its key and says it is not a CA certificate is `ca-bundle-7-not-a-ca`; the manifest names the break in their `flaw` (`not-signed-by-its-own-key`, `not-a-ca`), and the cases `ca-bundle-certificate-signed-by-another-key` and `ca-bundle-certificate-not-a-ca` refuse them with `ca-bundle-mismatch`. Each differs from `ca-bundle-7` in the certificate of A only. Three bundles differ from it in the certificates, and one in the first line: `ca-bundle-7-extra-certificate` (A, B and C), `ca-bundle-7-missing-certificate` (A only), `ca-bundle-7-wrong-order` (B, then A) and `ca-bundle-8-of-list-7` (the certificates of `seq7-a` under the first line `# trust-sequence: 8`); the cases `ca-bundle-with-a-certificate-too-many`, `ca-bundle-with-a-certificate-missing`, `ca-bundle-in-the-wrong-order` and `ca-bundle-with-the-wrong-first-line` refuse them with `ca-bundle-mismatch`, and the manifest names their flaw (`extra-certificate`, `missing-certificate`, `wrong-order`, `wrong-sequence`). `ca-bundle-7-issuer-is-another-name` has the key of A, is signed by it and is a CA certificate, and names another issuer than its subject (the flaw `issuer-not-subject`); `ca-bundle-certificate-names-another-issuer` refuses it with `ca-bundle-mismatch`: a root certificate names itself as its issuer.
- **The lowest sequence for initial pins** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 51; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). A case with `min_sequence` is a host that holds only its initial pins and was given a lowest sequence to accept (`--min-sequence N`); it has no held list. `initial-pins-lowest-sequence-above` (8, for a list of sequence 7) is refused with `rollback`; `initial-pins-lowest-sequence-equal` (7) is accepted.
- **What check 5 also refuses** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 49; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). Each list differs from `seq7-a` (or `seq8-b-without-a`) in one thing, is signed validly, and is refused with `malformed` against a held list; the manifest names the fault in its `flaw`: `label-twice` (`seq7-a-label-twice`, the label A twice), `pin-twice` (`seq7-a-pin-twice`), `fingerprint-wrong-form` (an upper-case OpenPGP fingerprint), `last-record-digest-wrong-form` (a digest of 63 digits), `sequence-0` (`seq0-a`, against initial pins: check 5 comes before the sequence), `pin-twice-in-removals` (`seq8-b-without-a-removal-twice`) and `empty-authorisation` (`seq8-b-without-a-empty-authorisation`). The cases carry the names of the faults.
- **The warning of an expired held list** is `held-expired` in the case `held-list-expired`, and in the like cases of the SSH CA key list set (`held-list-expired`) and the CRL set (`held-crl-expired`), as the pages name it. It was `expired` before.

`just check-vectors` also checks the dates of every list against its `flaw`, that each CA bundle certificate verifies with its own key and is a CA certificate unless its bundle has a `flaw`, and that the members `bundle` and `min_sequence` of a case agree with the list and the bundle it names.

The expected result of each case of this set was checked against the command `ritueel verify root-list` of the Go code on 2026-11-14 (run again for round 4 on the built command, with the CA bundle check) (the lists, the CA bundles and the lowest sequence; the clock of each case).

**Rules that have no vector yet**, and why:

- A signature file or a CA bundle of more than 256 KiB (and the read limit of 8 MiB), and a `root-list.json` of more than 256 KiB: a file that large does not belong in the tree.
- A signature by a key that is not P-384 (`signature-invalid`): a root key on a list is P-384 by the root profile, and the pin of a key that is not P-384 would have to be on the list the host holds; the generator makes only P-384 root keys.
- What the host does not enforce (the canonical form, `last_record_sha256` above sequence 1, the order of `roots` and `removals`, a removal entry's label, an empty `removals`) and an entry with no `openpgp_fingerprint`: these are accepted today and no case states them.
- The exit codes of the command for a file that is missing, a link, a FIFO or a folder, and which check a file over 256 KiB reaches: the manifest gives the outcome and the code of a check, not a failure of the command.
